handoff: Changes requested, 3 blocking: a comment on a block edge's outcome key is dropped; a # line ending a block scalar above type: is moved out of it; a like copy's agent: <name> is not renamed to by:. All ACs have tests and they pass.

findings.title: A comment on a block edge's outcome key is silently dropped
findings.detail:
When a block edge is left with only `to`, edgeEdits replaces everything from the outcome key's `:` to the end of the edge (`keyEnd = text.lastIndexOf(":", first.from)`). A trailing comment on the outcome key's line is in that range and disappears. Input: `outcomes:
  pass: # the happy path
    to: describe
    means: ok` (in an agent step) gives `pass: describe` with no comment. Also, if that comment holds a `:`, lastIndexOf finds the colon inside the comment. The check for comments at line 371 looks only at the edge's items, not the outcome key's own line. This breaks user story 36 ('keep every comment'), 37 (comment stays on its outcome's line) and AC7 ('a comment the translation leaves with no node to sit on … the file is refused').
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep the outcome key's trailing comment after the bare target (`pass: describe # the happy path`), or refuse the file at that line; add a test for it.

findings.title: A `#` line inside a block scalar above a removed key is moved out of the scalar
findings.detail:
spanOf takes any line above a key that starts with `#` and is indented at least as deep as the key as a leading comment. Text lines inside a block scalar written just above `type:` (or `action:`, `run:`, `prompt:`, `instructions:`) match too. Input: `a:
    description: |
      text
      # not a comment
    type: check
    run: bun test` gives `      # not a comment` above `check: bun test` and a description that has lost its last line. Shell scripts in `run: |` / `description: |` often hold `#` lines. This breaks D3a ('every untouched key keeps its text byte for byte') and AC2 ('none is re-wrapped or restyled … where a scalar cannot be kept as written, the file is refused').
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Take only real comment lines as leading comments, for example by stopping at the end of the previous pair's value range, or by using the `yaml` node's `commentBefore`. Add a test with a block scalar that ends in a `#` line just above `type:`.

findings.title: A `like` copy's `agent: <name>` is not renamed to `by:`
findings.detail:
`agent` is renamed to `by` only when the step has `type` (`if (typePair && agentName)`). An old-wording `like` copy can override the agent name (shared-workflow.ts merges copies shallowly), e.g. `review-codex: { like: review, agent: codex }` in a file whose other steps are old. That copy comes back unchanged. In the new wording, `agent: codex` is the copy's orientation, so the copy runs on the default agent with the orientation 'codex'. The same happens when the copy also writes `skill:`, which marks it as old. The JSON path (`k === "agent" && kind !== undefined`) has the same gap. This breaks user story 42 ('rename it to by: <name>, so that the step keeps running on the same agent') and AC6.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: When the file holds old-wording steps (D2: mixed counts as old), rename `agent` to `by` on `like` copies too, in both the YAML and JSON paths, and add a test. Or refuse the copy as ambiguous, naming its line.

findings.title: A YAML file that does not parse comes back as translated and unchanged
findings.detail:
`if (doc.errors.length) return text;` returns `{ ok: true, changed: false }` for a broken file, so `norn upgrade` (slice 08) would report it as already in the new wording, not as refused with a line. The loader will refuse it later anyway, so this is not a failure today.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse it with the first parse error's position, or decide in slice 08 that upgrade reports parse errors on its own.

findings.title: The comment on apply() says insertions go first, but removals are applied first
findings.detail:
When two edits start at the same place, the sort puts the removal before the insertion. That order is the correct one (an insertion applied first would then be removed), but the comment says the opposite.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Say that a removal is applied before an insertion at the same start, so the inserted text survives.
